summary.primary_unverified_bottleneck: Conservative 0.08 similarity margin in the absence of EXIF GPS coordinates despite high Top-1 similarity (0.80-0.94)
primary_retrieval_bottlenecks: Macro detail / lack of global building silhouette (split_c_002)
Interior statuary vs exterior facade mismatch (split_c_027)

specimens.root_cause_diagnosis: Dravidian / Nagara temple friezes and stone chariot reliefs yield ambiguous keypoint matches. RANSAC Top-1 inliers (10) are closely rivaled by competitor inliers (5).
specimens.architectural_explanation: Repetitive friezes, granite moldings, and temple plinths produce false geometric correspondence across 11th-13th century stone structures (Brihadeeswarar vs Konark vs Hampi).
specimens.remediation_strategy: Enforce strict inlier threshold (>= 12) AND inlier spatial spread check (dispersion > 0.40 frame width) to prevent false positive homographies on repetitive stone relief.

specimens.root_cause_diagnosis: Margin is 0.0750 (just below 0.08 threshold). Top-1 inliers: 7. Competitor inliers: 5. Gatekeeper: 0.7192.
specimens.architectural_explanation: Facade features (e.g. Hawa Mahal honeycombed jharokhas, Charminar illuminated arches, Sanchi torana) have distinctive silhouettes but smooth or low-light regions reduce sparse keypoints.
specimens.remediation_strategy: Combine margin relaxation with local CLIP patch confirmation (>= 0.80) to safely verify without relying solely on sparse SIFT.

specimens.root_cause_diagnosis: Clear distinctive architectural geometry (Charminar minarets) yields 22 RANSAC inliers. Margin was 0.0657 (below 0.08) purely due to high baseline CLIP similarity across stone arches. Safely corroborable via SIFT.
specimens.architectural_explanation: Prominent 4-minaret structural silhouette and stucco relief provide invariant corner keypoints matching ref_01/ref_04.
specimens.remediation_strategy: Policy B / Policy D relaxes margin floor to 0.05 when RANSAC inliers >= 10, enabling safe automatic verification.

specimens.root_cause_diagnosis: Extreme macro close-up of granite temple frieze. Global CLIP embedding lacks temple vimana silhouette and classifies granite carving texture as Konark chlorite relief.
specimens.architectural_explanation: Granite relief carving of Chola dvarapala without vimana roof profile resembles eastern Ganga dynasty chlorite reliefs in stone texture and lighting.
specimens.remediation_strategy: Expand reference gallery to include localized carving crops and regional anchor vectors.

specimens.root_cause_diagnosis: Low-angle viewpoint heavily occluded by tourists, umbrellas, and waterfront barricades. Basalt arch structure is truncated.
specimens.architectural_explanation: Over 50% of the lower image area consists of pedestrian crowd and reflective promenade pavers, causing CLIP to match Sanchi stupa crowd photos.
specimens.remediation_strategy: Implement upper-half salient region cropping when foreground crowd density is detected.

specimens.root_cause_diagnosis: Extreme worm's-eye view looking straight up the fluted sandstone shaft. Circular projection mimics Konark wheel spokes in global embedding.
specimens.architectural_explanation: Conical fluting viewed from base converges radially, producing radial geometric features identical to sun temple chariot wheels.
specimens.remediation_strategy: Incorporate radial vertical projection augmentation during reference indexing.

specimens.root_cause_diagnosis: Very distant view across Mumbai harbor under heavy marine haze. CLIP embedding has very low similarity (< 0.56) across all classes; correctly rejected from false verification.
specimens.architectural_explanation: Contrast ratio < 1.4:1; architectural edges washed out by marine humidity and air pollution.
specimens.remediation_strategy: Implement CLAHE contrast enhancement pre-processing before embedding extraction.

specimens.root_cause_diagnosis: Rear courtyard view of Hawa Mahal. All 20 reference gallery images capture the iconic pink honeycombed street facade.
specimens.architectural_explanation: Hawa Mahal rear facade consists of plain yellow-washed courtyards and open pillared verandas without the iconic jharokha screens.
specimens.remediation_strategy: Expand reference gallery from 20 to 30 views per monument to cover non-iconic rear courtyards.

specimens.root_cause_diagnosis: Distant night photograph with artificial yellow spot illumination. Charminar's illuminated night views matched closer.
specimens.architectural_explanation: White marble reflects yellow floodlights, shifting color distribution into Charminar granite illumination domain.
specimens.remediation_strategy: Add illumination-invariant color normalization and nighttime reference gallery views.

specimens.root_cause_diagnosis: Interior bronze/marble sculpture group inside Queen's Hall. Reference gallery strictly contains exterior palace views.
specimens.architectural_explanation: Interior allegorical statuary lacks classical Renaissance dome and garden water reflection features present in gallery.
specimens.remediation_strategy: Domain boundary rule: explicitly classify interior museum exhibits as INTERIOR_EXHIBIT requiring dedicated exhibit index.
